title: Coalescer scheduling leads to slab misalignment and fp-accumulation bias in streaming decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Intermittent correctness failures observed in streaming decode under mixed-batch coalescing. Symptoms include subtle token reorderings in long-prefix scenarios, occasionally corrupted KV slab pointers in a small subset of requests, and small but measurable floating-point accumulation bias that diverges across runs. This appears to be correlated with the coalescer's micro-batching of prefill and decode lanes when using the adaptive scheduler on GPUs with heterogeneous sequence lengths.

Why it matters: These errors are reproducible on customer workloads hitting Dedicated pools and cause downstream hallucinations and nondeterministic diffs in evals. Production incidents (see incident links) drove urgency; impact is customer-visible in the form of token inconsistencies and rare token truncation.

Scope: Observed on runs using runtime-1.20/1.21 and repro'd locally with the adaptive coalescer enabled. Affects mixture-of-length batched traffic and workloads that use prefix caching (KV cache warm paths). Not observed in single-request decode or fully synchronized batch paths.
steps_to_reproduce: Enable adaptive coalescer with mixed sequence length workloads (prefixes between 64-2048 tokens)
Run streaming prefill concurrently with small decode batches (prefill arrival skew ~5-30ms)
Use model variants with fused attention kernels and mixed-precision enabled (fp16 math + bf16 accumulators)
Collect outputs across multiple runs (>=1000 requests) and diff token sequences for nondeterminism
Capture per-request KV slab pointers and prefill/decode scheduling timestamps via the runtime trace flags
investigation_log: 2026-03-01: Customer report received; reproduced locally against runtime-1.21 on p4-16g with synthetic traffic using seed corpus from customer. Noted rare token reorders and small numeric deltas in softmax accumulators.

2026-03-03: Added extra tracing in coalescer (coalesce.debug=true) and KV slab allocator to log slab base/tail pointers. Observed transient slab pointer offsets when a prefill worker yielded mid-coalesce.

2026-03-05: A/B test: disabled adaptive coalescer -> no repro. Re-enabled with strict serial coalescing (no lane interleaving) -> repro rate drops to near zero. Confirms scheduler/coalescer interaction.

2026-03-07: Reproduced in unit test harness by introducing prefill scheduling jitter and forcing an interleaving of memory writes; observed accumulation differences in the final softmax which explain token probability shifts.

2026-03-09: Profiling shows a race between the coalescer shadow-warmup path and KV slab rotation: warmup can rotate slab pointers while decode lane still referencing prior slot when micro-batching merges lanes, producing a stale pointer deref leading to partial overwrite of shared slab region.

2026-03-11: Confirmed floating-point accumulation bias stems from non-associative reduction ordering across coalesced micro-batches; kernel selection logic switches between two reduction kernels depending on inferred lane homogeneity causing divergent rounding order.
2026-03-12: Drafted patch to serialize slab rotation with a lightweight epoch/sequence and to normalize reduction ordering across kernels. Preparing PR and safety rollout plan.
root_cause: A combination of coalescer micro-batching interleaving and an unsynchronized slab rotation path allowed decode lanes to reference stale KV slots while the allocator moved base offsets. Simultaneously, kernel selector chose a different reduction implementation for coalesced vs homogeneous batches, producing a consistent-but-different rounding order that accumulates bias over long prefixes. The concurrency window is small, so failures are low-frequency but high-impact.
proposed_fix: 1) Add an epoch-based guard to the KV slab allocator so any slab rotation increments an epoch visible to coalescer/delivery paths; lanes must check/stabilize epoch before dereferencing slot pointers. 2) Force the kernel selector to use a single deterministic reduction implementation for all micro-batched streaming decode codepaths (config flag runtime.coalescer.force_deterministic_reduction=true). 3) Add unit and fuzz tests that simulate prefill/decode interleaving and validate slab pointer stability and bitwise-identical decode on deterministic mode.
tests_added: unit: coalescer_epoch_stability_test (reproduces slab pointer race with injected jitter)
integration: mixed_length_streaming_determinism (1000-request smoke to assert identical outputs across runs)
fuzz: kv_allocator_rotate_fuzz (randomized slab rotations while streaming)
validation_plan: Run CI with added unit/integration tests, run canary on Dedicated pool with adaptive coalescer disabled then enabled in deterministic mode, monitor per-request diffs and KV pointer stability. Target < 0.01% repro rate before wide rollout. Use nightly eval harness (reference prompts) to ensure numerical parity with baseline where deterministic reduction is enabled.
rollback_strategy: If regressions in latency/throughput are observed, revert kernel selector change and instead keep slab epoch guard only while we iterate on deterministic reduction performance. Ability to toggle runtime.coalescer.force_deterministic_reduction via config without restart for rapid rollback.
deployment_plan: 1) Merge PR to eng/next after two approvals and perf-signoff. 2) Canary to Dedicated pool subset (10% capacity) with detailed tracing enabled for 48h. 3) Gradual 25/50/100 rollout with health gates (token-error-rate, decode-latency-p50/p95, token-diff-rate).
notes: Trade-offs: forcing deterministic reduction may have a ~1-3% perf regression on some hardware; we will profile and if unacceptable, implement a fast-path deterministic reducer optimized for common shapes. Also need to audit other allocators for similar epoch-free rotations. Coordination required with Dedicated ops to schedule canary.
